newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hysan to benefit from rising rentals - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Hysan to benefit from rising rentals - analysts.

text.p: Hong Kong property developer and investor Hysan Development Ltd was well positioned to benefit from rising rental prices for luxury residential and office properties, analysts said on Thursday.

The company is forecast to report earnings growth of around seven to 10 percent when it announces results for the six months to June 30 on Friday, and analysts expect to see increases of 11 percent to 20 percent for the full year.
"Hysan is my top pick in the investment property sector," said Raymond Ngai, senior research analyst at UBS Securities (East Asia) Ltd.
Hysan reported net profit of HK$632 million (US$81.8 million) in the six months to June 1995 and HK$1.23 billion for the full year.

Ngai said Hysan has a portfolio of high quality properties and greater relative exposure to the luxury residential sector than any other listed property company, with about 25 percent of its holdings in terms of gross floor area in that sector.
Limited new supply in luxury residential property on Hong Kong island in 1996 and 1997 should ensure good rental rates and capital appreciation in the coming 12 to 18 months, he said.
This in turn should yield good appreciation in capital values, meaning Hysan will achieve faster growth in its total net asset value (NAV), he added.
"Hysan's appraised NAV (per share) in 1995 was HK$29.70 and I estimate a rise to HK$33.60 in 1996," Ngai said, noting that was the highest NAV growth in the property sector.
Yuen Weir, property analyst at Merrill Lynch, agreed.
"Hysan is a quality play, which has seen its share price move up more in line with its NAV," said Weir.
But because of the share's recent rise, its discount to NAV is tight relative to other property investment companies, leading Merrill to downgrade it one notch to accumulate from buy, he added.
Hysan shares have jumped some 15 percent since the end of July, handily outperforming the blue-chip Hang Seng index. The shares were trading at HK$24.20 Thursday afternoon, up HK$0.15.
Weir also predicted the group's office properties, the Caroline Center and Lee Gardens redevelopment, would fuel a good part of Hysan's growth.
"Caroline Center was completed in late 1992 and fully let before the big upswing in rental rates, thus the majority of rental contracts will be signed and renewed in 1996 at higher rates," he said.
Ngai forecast net profit growth of 9.8 percent at the interim stage, with the total boosted by gains from share investments, and 13.4 percent for the full year.

One local brokerage analyst said Hysan would get a quarter of its earnings from interest income and its share portfolio, predicting net profit growth of seven percent at the interim and 11 percent for the full year.
Merrill's Weir forecast 20 percent net profit growth for the full year 1996. (US$1=HK$7.73)
